title: Service Workers and the Cache API

options.text: A background script that acts as a programmable network proxy, intercepting fetch requests
A faster kind of web server
A CSS feature for offline styling

questions.explanation: A service worker runs in the background as a programmable proxy between the page and the network, handling requests via the fetch event. It requires HTTPS and has no DOM access.

questions.prompt: Match each caching strategy to its behaviour.

pairs.right: Serve from cache, fall back to the network
Try the network, fall back to the cache
Serve cache now, update it in the background

questions.explanation: Cache-first suits immutable assets, network-first suits fresh content, stale-while-revalidate balances the two, and cache-only serves fixed content offline.

questions.prompt: A service worker will only register over ____ (except on localhost).
questions.explanation: Because a service worker can intercept all requests, it requires a secure context (HTTPS); localhost is exempted for development.

questions.prompt: Does a service worker speed up the FIRST visit to a site?

options.text: Yes, it caches everything before the page loads
No — it installs during or after the first load, so it accelerates subsequent visits
Only if the page uses HTTP/3

questions.explanation: The service worker installs during/after the first load, so the first visit sees no benefit; it speeds up repeat visits and enables offline.

questions.prompt: Which statements about service workers are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: You should version caches and delete old ones on activate
A service worker cannot access the DOM directly
A service worker makes the first visit instant
With the Cache API it can serve content offline

questions.explanation: Version and clean up caches, remember there's no DOM access, and use the Cache API for offline. It does not speed the first visit.

questions.prompt: Order the main stages of the service worker lifecycle.

items.text: Register the service worker from the page
Intercept fetch events for controlled pages

questions.explanation: The page registers it; it installs (precaching), activates (cleaning old caches), then begins handling fetch events for the pages it controls.
